title: Universal ring-sheaf scalar extension with normalized resolution comparisons
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a site small relative to a chosen module universe, $\mathcal O,\mathcal O'$ sheaves of commutative rings on it, and $\varphi:\mathcal O\to\mathcal O'$ a ring-sheaf homomorphism. Use the abelian categories of module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], their unbounded homotopy and derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], and localization functors $Q:K(\mathcal O)\to D(\mathcal O)$ and $Q':K(\mathcal O')\to D(\mathcal O')$ in sufficiently large universes. Let $T$ be termwise sheaf extension of scalars $-\otimes_{\mathcal O}\mathcal O'$ [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product] and put $F=Q'T$. Let $\mathcal P$ be the class of all K-flat $\mathcal O$-complexes [def-pc-kflat-complex], without a termwise-flatness restriction. Then $F$ is an exact functor of triangulated categories, every complex has a resolution from $\mathcal P$, and $F$ inverts every quasi-isomorphism between members of $\mathcal P$. There exists a pair $(L,\varepsilon)$ with $L:D(\mathcal O)\to D(\mathcal O')$ exact and $\varepsilon:LQ\to F$ natural, such that for every functor $H:D(\mathcal O)\to D(\mathcal O')$ the map $\alpha\mapsto\varepsilon\circ(\alpha Q)$ is a bijection $\operatorname{Nat}(H,L)\cong\operatorname{Nat}(HQ,F)$, and $\varepsilon_P$ is invertible for every $P\in\mathcal P$. Its functor agrees with the derived change of rings of [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings] through the unique isomorphism respecting the universal counits.

For any such universal pair and any K-flat resolution $q:P\to X$, the morphism
$$\theta_q=\varepsilon_P\circ L(Qq)^{-1}:L(QX)\xrightarrow{\sim}F(P)$$
is an isomorphism in $D(\mathcal O')$ and $\varepsilon_X=F(q)\circ\theta_q$. If $q':P'\to X'$, $a:X\to X'$ and $b:P\to P'$ obey $q'b=aq$, then $F(b)\circ\theta_q=\theta_{q'}\circ L(Qa)$. For two resolutions of the same $X$, the canonical comparison is $\theta_{q'}\circ\theta_q^{-1}$; these comparisons are compatible with augmentation to $F(X)$ and satisfy the identity and three-resolution cocycle equations. These formulas hold for every universal pair, via its unique counit-compatible isomorphism, and impose neither flatness of $\varphi$ nor boundedness of complexes.

proof.text: Write $E(M)=M\otimes_{\mathcal O}\mathcal O'$ for ordinary sheaf scalar extension. It is additive: on presheaf tensor generators, $((f+g)\otimes1)(m\otimes s)=f(m)\otimes s+g(m)\otimes s$, and the zero-map formula is the same calculation; the equalities extend by linearity and sheafification. The sheaf-module categories are abelian by [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], since the site is small relative to the module universe. Thus [lem-trf-additive-homotopy-triangulated] applies to $E$, giving the termwise functor $T=K(E)$ with its canonical exact triangulated structure. The localization $Q'$ is exact by [lem-pur-homotopy-category-triangulated], so $F=Q'T$ is exact. Here additivity comes from the actual sheafified tensor construction [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]; exactness on the abelian module categories is unnecessary.

source.place: Tag 014X (lemma-additive-exact-homotopy-category); sites-cohomology.tex Tag 06YY, opening of proof

proof.text: Take $\mathcal P$ to be all K-flat complexes, with the resolution convention of [def-pc-kflat-complex]. The resolution of any $X$ supplied by [lem-pc-kflat-resolution] has K-flat source, so belongs to $\mathcal P$; the stronger flat-terms conclusion of that lemma need not be imposed on other members of $\mathcal P$. For every quasi-isomorphism $s:P\to P'$ with $P,P'\in\mathcal P$, [lem-pur-change-of-rings-kflat-quasi-iso] applies to this actual additive $E$ and makes $T(s)$ a quasi-isomorphism. Since $Q'$ is localization at quasi-isomorphisms [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], $F(s)$ is invertible. These statements apply to arbitrary unbounded complexes and arbitrary $\varphi$.

source.place: Tags 06YS (lemma-K-flat-resolution) and 06YT (lemma-derived-tor-quasi-isomorphism-other-side); fixed-site specialization of Tag 06YY

proof.text: Apply [lem-pur-left-derived-from-kflat-class] with $\mathcal A=\operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal O)$, target $D(\mathcal O')$, the exact $F$ of step 1, and the class of step 2. Its two hypotheses are precisely the resolution and inversion assertions just proved. It gives an exact $L:D(\mathcal O)\to D(\mathcal O')$ and $\varepsilon:LQ\to F$, with $\varepsilon_P$ invertible for every $P\in\mathcal P$. Its right-Kan universal property says that each natural transformation $HQ\to F$ factors through $\varepsilon$ by a unique $H\to L$. This is exactly the stated bijection, with the map $\alpha\mapsto\varepsilon\circ(\alpha Q)$, for every functor $H$; no exactness of $H$ is required.

source.place: Tag 06XN (lemma-find-existence-computes), dual part; equation-everywhere and Tag 05SE (proposition-derived-functor)

proof.text: Let $(M,\eta)$ be another universal pair for the same $F,Q$, in particular the left derived change of rings of [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings]. Universality gives unique $u:L\to M$ and $v:M\to L$ with $\eta\circ(uQ)=\varepsilon$ and $\varepsilon\circ(vQ)=\eta$. Consequently $vu$ and $1_L$ have the same composite with $\varepsilon$ after precomposition by $Q$, so injectivity in the universal property gives $vu=1_L$; likewise $uv=1_M$. This proves the unique counit-compatible isomorphism. It also shows that any pair satisfying the universal property inherits invertibility of its counit on every K-flat complex from the pair of step 3. Thus the next calculations may start with any universal pair.

source.place: Tag 05S9 (definition-right-derived-functor-defined), left-derived convention, and equation-everywhere; sites-cohomology.tex Tag 06YY

proof.text: Fix a K-flat resolution $q:P\to X$. By localization, $Qq$ is invertible, hence so is $L(Qq)$. Define $\theta_q=\varepsilon_P\circ L(Qq)^{-1}$; both factors are invertible. Naturality of $\varepsilon$ for $q$ gives $F(q)\circ\varepsilon_P=\varepsilon_X\circ L(Qq)$. Composing on the right with $L(Qq)^{-1}$ proves $F(q)\circ\theta_q=\varepsilon_X$. This does not assert that $F(q)$ itself is invertible when $X$ is not K-flat.

source.place: Equation-everywhere, naturality of the universal left-derived counit and cancellation of the localized resolution

proof.text: For $q':P'\to X'$ and $q'b=aq$, functoriality and invertibility of $L(Qq),L(Qq')$ give $L(Qb)\circ L(Qq)^{-1}=L(Qq')^{-1}\circ L(Qa)$. Naturality at $b$ gives $F(b)\circ\varepsilon_P=\varepsilon_{P'}\circ L(Qb)$. Substitute these two equations to obtain $F(b)\circ\theta_q=\varepsilon_{P'}\circ L(Qb)\circ L(Qq)^{-1}=\theta_{q'}\circ L(Qa)$. Neither $a$ nor $b$ is assumed invertible.

source.place: Equation-everywhere, naturality of the counit; explicit algebra of the commuting augmentation square

proof.text: For resolutions $q_i:P_i\to X$ put $c_{ij}=\theta_{q_j}\circ\theta_{q_i}^{-1}$. Then $c_{ii}=1$ and $c_{jk}\circ c_{ij}=\theta_{q_k}\circ\theta_{q_i}^{-1}=c_{ik}$ by cancellation. Step 5 gives $F(q_j)\circ c_{ij}=\varepsilon_X\circ\theta_{q_i}^{-1}=F(q_i)$, proving augmentation compatibility. For any map $b:P_i\to P_j$ over $X$, step 6 with $a=1_X$ gives $F(b)=c_{ij}$. The definition of $c_{ij}$ requires no chosen map between resolutions.

source.place: Equation-everywhere; sites-cohomology.tex Tag 06YY, resolution computation, with explicit identity and cocycle equations

proof.text: Finally let $u:L\xrightarrow{\sim}M$ be the counit-compatible isomorphism of step 4. From $\eta_Pu_{QP}=\varepsilon_P$ and naturality $u_{QP}L(Qq)^{-1}=M(Qq)^{-1}u_{QX}$ one obtains $\theta_q^{L}=\theta_q^{M}u_{QX}$. Hence $\theta_{q_j}^{L}(\theta_{q_i}^{L})^{-1}=\theta_{q_j}^{M}(\theta_{q_i}^{M})^{-1}$. The augmentation and square equations of steps 5 and 6 therefore hold in each pair and are identified by $u$. This proves the asserted independence of the universal presentation. All inverses used above are counits on K-flat objects or images of quasi-isomorphisms under localization; none uses flatness of $\varphi$ or boundedness.

source.place: Equation-everywhere and uniqueness in Tag 05S9, explicit counit-compatible change of universal pair
